insight: The loader.ts frontmatter parser for persona .md files was extended to handle a nested map-of-arrays (premountedTools) by tracking an inPremountMode state plus currentPremountPlugin. The key insight is that the parser uses indentation to distinguish top-level keys from nested plugin-id keys under premountedTools, and it properly flushes state at boundaries. This pattern generalizes well for future nested YAML structures in persona frontmatter.

When adding a new required method to DronePluginRegistration (like listMountedTools), all mock registration objects in test files must be updated. Using sed to add the property after unmountTool worked but created duplicates when the same line pattern appeared multiple times with different indentation levels. A better approach would be to use a shared helper or spread pattern to construct mock registrations, reducing the number of files needing updates when the interface changes.

When adding a new debug subsystem that must be consumed by the plugin engine (e.g. `--debug tools`), the debug set cannot live privately in the conversation service because the engine is constructed before the conversation service in index.tsx. Extract a shared `DebugFlagRegistry` in drone-core (mirroring `RuntimeFlagRegistry`), created once in index.tsx and passed to both the engine and conversation service. This makes runtime toggling via `/debug` take effect in both layers and makes future debug flags trivial to add.

The drone-agent package resolves drone-core from its built dist/ (package.json "types": "./dist/index.d.ts"), not from source. So after editing drone-core types, you MUST run `pnpm -r run build` before LSP/typecheck in dependent packages reflects the change; otherwise you'll chase stale diagnostics.

conversation-service.ts executes all tool calls in a single assistant turn in parallel via Promise.all (line ~419). Any plugin tool that does read-modify-write on a shared resource (e.g. a JSON file) will race itself when the LLM emits multiple calls to the same target in one turn. Plugin file writers must serialize (in-process per-key mutex) AND use tmp+rename atomic writes, because .drone-agent files aren't always checked into VCS so there's no external safety net. This bit self-improvement (recordInsight/storePrinciple/deletePrinciple); the memory plugin's writeMemoryEntry already used tmp+rename but NOT a mutex.

The project wiki (Obsidian vault at /home/unleet/Obsidian/drone-agent-project) is a separate git repo from the codebase. When ingesting work into the wiki: (1) diff from meta.json's last_commit to HEAD to find new commits; (2) bug fixes with a design choice go in decisions/ as ADRs (per meta/decision-bug-fixes-go-in-decisions.md), not concepts/; (3) update the affected concept/module pages, index.md, log.md, and advance meta.json; (4) commit the wiki repo separately. The .obsidian/workspace.json UI-state churn is tracked and committed alongside wiki content. Completed plans are deleted from project memory and that deletion is committed in the codebase repo.

When threading a new optional parameter through a shared execution interface (e.g. DroneToolDefinition.execute gaining a `context` param), the parameter must be propagated through EVERY layer: the core type, the engine interface, the engine implementation, the conversation service's executeToolSafely wrapper, AND the DroneSlashCommandContext type. Missing any one layer causes a typecheck/build failure that's only caught when running `pnpm run typecheck` (root) — the `pnpm -r run typecheck` per-package check alone won't catch test-file type errors. Always run the ROOT `pnpm run typecheck` (which includes tsconfig.test.json) in addition to the per-package recursive check.

The file__apply_diff tool matched the wrong `continue;` statement when applying a diff near the end of the conversation-service tool-call block. The hunk context `\n          continue;\n        }` was too generic and matched an earlier occurrence. The fix: include MORE distinctive surrounding context (like the `[Image from ${result.name} tool]` block) in the diff hunk, or use file__read + file__write for surgical edits near ambiguous control-flow keywords.

When an "estimate" function and an "actual execution" function must agree on the same semantics (e.g. evaluateSafetyTrim's drop-count estimate vs dropOldestNonSummaryTurns' actual drop), extract the shared logic into ONE pure helper used by both, rather than duplicating the rule in each. This is the review-state #8 fix: the estimate sliced turns from the front including summary turns while the actual drop stopped at the first summary turn, so the estimate overcounted droppable turns and the ensureSafeBudget while(true) loop could fail to converge and hard-fail with "no turns could be dropped". Extracting getDroppableTurnPrefix into turn-utils.ts and using it in both places guarantees they can never diverge again. General lesson: any time two code paths must stay in lockstep on a rule, a single shared pure function is the durable fix — not just patching one side to match the other.

When adding a trust gate to a shared client (e.g. gating coordinator-client sync methods behind a "swarm ready" flag), existing unit tests that exercise those methods will silently short-circuit and fail with "spy not called" unless the test setup establishes the trusted state. Sweep the test file's beforeEach and set up the gate state (e.g. confirm fingerprint + set beacon approved) so the gated methods actually run. This is the gap-1 TOFU fix: gating fetchPersonas/fetchSkills/pushEvents etc. broke 8 coordinator-client tests until the beforeEach was updated to mark the swarm ready.

When editing a single-line template literal that contains the CLI --help text (e.g. drone-coordinator/src/index.ts and drone-beacon/src/index.ts), inserting a new line via apply_diff can land the added text OUTSIDE the template literal (as a stray statement before console.log) rather than inside it. After any help-text edit, re-read the file to confirm the new line is actually inside the backtick string, and prefer replacing the whole template literal line in one hunk rather than inserting a separate line.

When extending a shared pure function's signature (e.g. generateVerificationCode from 2 to 3 inputs), the coordinator and beacon packages resolve drone-swarm-common from its built dist/ (package.json "types": "./dist/index.d.ts"), not from source. After editing drone-swarm-common/src, run `pnpm --filter drone-swarm-common run build` BEFORE running dependent-package tests (drone-coordinator, drone-beacon), or the tests will use the stale 2-arg dist and fail with type errors. This is the gap-2 bidirectional verification change.

A CI-only typecheck failure can be masked locally by stale dist/ artifacts. When a feature branch is based on an older commit, its drone-swarm-common/src/tls.ts may still be synchronous while main has since made loadOrCreateTlsIdentity async (openssl shell-injection fix #54). Locally, dependent packages (drone-coordinator, drone-beacon) resolve drone-swarm-common from its built dist/ (package.json "types": "./dist/tls.d.ts"), so a stale dist hides the mismatch and `pnpm typecheck` passes. CI does a fresh build and fails with "Property 'fingerprint' does not exist on type 'Promise<TlsIdentity>'". To reproduce locally, build drone-swarm-common from main's tls.ts (git show origin/main:... > src/tls.ts, rebuild, typecheck dependents), then restore. Lesson: when a branch predates a change to a shared dependency's signature, verify against the dependency's CURRENT (main) signature, not just the local dist.
